reasons: wp-admin's PHP screens, list tables, meta boxes and settings pages. React-WP's admin is React: a plugin adds a screen with rwp_add_menu_page, content with a slot, a card with an Integrations card, a check with a setup check.
Reads and writes the server's disk. React-WP is deployed from Git and updated by commits.
React-WP keeps no revision history, autosave or edit lock on pages.
The classic editor (TinyMCE), WordPress's upload UI, image sub-sizes and oEmbed are not part of React-WP; files go through the Media Library and rich text through the TipTap editor.
React-WP is one site per Supabase project. Multisite networks do not exist.
A standalone PHP entry point (wp-mail.php, wp-signup.php, trackbacks). React-WP has no such endpoints.
Plugins are installed, activated and removed from the Plugins screen (and by commits), not by PHP hooks.

PHP template files and the template hierarchy. A theme is a Theme Editor layout plus Site Templates; template tags are React components. The few that fit (the title, the content, the excerpt, body classes) are implemented.
Post formats and the Links manager do not exist in React-WP.
Pings, trackbacks and enclosures do not exist in React-WP.
A site option is an ordinary option here (see the option hooks); autoload and the Settings API are not part of React-WP.

A veto or rewrite point inside WordPress's PHP save routine (the database applies row level security after the request, so a browser callback cannot veto it), or a feature React-WP does not have (post hierarchy, redirects for old slugs, the block editor, pings).
Account lifecycle, passwords, nonces, sessions and notification emails belong to Supabase Auth and the server. The sign-in hooks that exist are rwp_login, rwp_logout and rwp_user_register.
Comment forms, flood control, cookies and trash. React-WP's Comments section is a React component; comments are approved, pending or spam.
The PHP wp-login.php and registration pages. React-WP's sign-in screens are React; use rwp_login, rwp_logout, rwp_user_register and the floating-login settings.
Keyed on a wp-admin PHP file name. React-WP admin screens are not PHP files; use the screen id.
PHP's request bootstrap: wpdb, constants, object cache, query parsing, rewrite rules. React-WP has no PHP request.
admin-ajax.php and admin-post.php do not exist. A plugin registers a server route instead.
Accounts, passwords and mail are handled by Supabase Auth and the server, not by PHP hooks.
Belongs to a plugin bundled with WordPress (Akismet, Hello Dolly), not to core.
WordPress's personal-data tools and application passwords do not exist; see Settings → Backup and Supabase Auth.
Comment form markup, flood control and notification emails are handled by the Comments section, the database policies and the server.
Gutenberg's block system. The Page Builder replaces it; its widgets are registered with the builder's own API, not with register_block_type.
These shape the SQL of WordPress's database layer. React-WP queries through PostgREST; use rwp_pre_get_posts to change a query.
Feed and robots.txt output written by PHP. React-WP serves /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml from server routes.

The Media Library stores files at a provider (Cloudinary, ImageKit) and serves them from there: there is no local upload pipeline, image editor, resize step, embed or gallery shortcode of WordPress's.
Feeds, bookmarks, shortlinks and canonical-link headers are not produced by PHP here.
The PHP Loop and its markup printers. React renders a list by mapping over an array (rwp_get_posts).
There is no PHP REST server. Data comes from PostgREST through client.from(); server-side work is a route in the plugin's server.mjs.
Transport settings of PHP's HTTP client. The browser's fetch applies its own redirect, TLS and CORS rules.
The PHP widget classes and sidebars. A widget is a Page Builder widget or a Theme Editor block.
RSS/Atom feed generation is not implemented. Open a request if a site needs it.
PHP-printed asset tags, block assets and Heartbeat. Scripts and styles are added to the document at runtime (rwp_enqueue_script).
wp-admin list tables, bulk and quick edit boxes. React-WP's admin screens are React components.
Walker classes and per-item markup filters of wp_nav_menu. rwp_nav_menu renders a fixed structure; its rwp_nav_menu_objects, rwp_nav_menu_items and rwp_nav_menu filters change it.
Gettext .mo/.po loading and language packs. Translations are dictionaries and Settings → Translations rows.
WordPress's per-request query caches have no equivalent in React-WP.
The Customizer is a PHP preview framework. The Theme Editor takes its place.
Term-table internals, per-field save filters and PHP-path or admin-URL helpers with no React-WP counterpart.
There is no wp-cron. Scheduled work is a plugin server.mjs route called by a platform cron.
PHP/MySQL health tests. The Dashboard → Overview checklist is the counterpart.
Emoji, smilies, kses and typography internals; use rwp_kses_post, rwptexturize and rwp_sprintf.
A placeholder name used inside WordPress documentation.
WordPress's installer, importers and update screens. React-WP has a Setup Wizard, Updates and Backup of its own.

SQL and cache internals of WordPress's meta tables. Meta is rwp_meta rows read through PostgREST.
Deprecated in WordPress. A new API should not carry deprecated names.
Multisite, or WordPress's own installer. React-WP has its Setup Wizard and a single site per project.
XML-RPC is a PHP server protocol. React-WP exposes PostgREST and server routes instead.
Mail and account creation belong to the server and Supabase Auth.
WordPress platform subsystems (HTML API, Interactivity API, Abilities, AI client, fonts) with no React-WP counterpart.
A third-party PHP library bundled with WordPress, not a WordPress API.
A private WordPress internal (leading underscore). WordPress itself tells plugins not to call it.
React-WP keeps no revision history, autosave or edit lock on pages. The Page Builder has its own autosave.
Feeds, bookmarks (the Links manager), shortlinks and canonical-link headers are not generated by React-WP's PHP-free server; SEO tags are written by server/seo.mjs and src/lib/seo.ts.
Post formats do not exist in React-WP.
WordPress's personal-data export/erase tools. Use Settings → Backup and the Supabase dashboard.
The WordPress Links manager (blogroll) does not exist.
Plugins are installed, activated, paused and removed from the Plugins screen and by commits, not from code; rwp_get_plugins and rwp_is_plugin_active read their state.
Theme features are chosen in the Theme Editor and Settings, not declared in PHP. Menus, widget areas and image sizes are configured there.
A wp-admin PHP form helper. The React-WP admin screens are React components.
Roles are fixed in src/lib/roles.ts and granted under Settings → Roles; there is no multisite, user counts cache or contact-method list.
The Settings API generates PHP forms and saves them through options.php. Build the form in React and save with rwp_update_option (public values only).
Navigation links between list pages are React components; use rwp_paginate_links, rwp_get_previous_post and rwp_get_next_post.
PHP login-page and account-email internals. Sign-in is React-WP's own login screen on Supabase Auth.
PHP response headers and HTML printers; see the matching rwp_ function where one exists.
kses, entity and emoji internals, SQL sanitisers and shortcode regex helpers. Use rwp_kses, rwp_kses_post, rwptexturize and rwp_do_shortcode.
Server configuration (.htaccess, web.config, PHP ini, disk permissions). React-WP is deployed from Git.
PHP polyfills. JavaScript and TypeScript provide these natively.
WordPress's image pipeline (sub-sizes, srcset, editors, EXIF, embeds, galleries, captions). Files live at the storage provider; rwp_get_attachment_image returns an for the original.
The PHP render callback of one built-in Gutenberg block. The Page Builder renders its own widgets.
WordPress's per-request query caches. React-WP reads through PostgREST and has no equivalent cache to prime.
Comment markup is rendered by the Comments section (a React component with theme blocks), not printed by PHP.
Admin-form term helpers, term-count caches and HTML renderers (tag cloud, category list). A theme builds these from rwp_get_terms() as React.
Nonces protect PHP forms from cross-site requests. React-WP sends a signed session token with every request (Supabase Auth) and the database enforces access, so there is no nonce.
React-WP has no page hierarchy, post passwords, future-post scheduler, old-slug redirects or query-variable layer of WordPress's PHP request.
Comment flood control, notifications and cookies are handled by the database policies and the server, not by PHP.
Accounts and passwords are Supabase Auth. Sign-in, registration and password reset have no PHP counterpart; the hooks fire around them (rwp_login, rwp_user_register).
React-WP stores no commenter IP, has no comment trash (a comment is approved, pending or spam) and edits through rwp_update_comment.
Includes a PHP template file. In React-WP a theme is a layout and a Site Template; register a component instead.
Addresses of PHP theme, plugin and include folders. React-WP bundles its assets, so there is no such path.
Option autoloading and priming are WordPress object-cache concerns; options here are read on demand.
Meta boxes are PHP panels on the post editor. The editor is a React screen; a plugin adds its own admin page or a Page Builder control.
SimplePie, a bundled PHP feed parser.
WordPress's default script/style registry, block assets and fonts. Scripts and styles are queued with rwp_enqueue_script and rwp_enqueue_style.
Builds SQL for WordPress's database layer. React-WP queries through PostgREST.
Registered menu locations and menu-item posts. React-WP has one location column per menu (rwp_get_nav_menu_locations).
Media upload, embed and image-processing internals of WordPress's PHP media pipeline. Uploads go to the storage provider from the Media Library.
Files live at the storage provider and are added or removed in the Media Library, which also deletes the provider copy. There is no local file path.
An internal of the avatar and preferences systems; use rwp_get_avatar and rwp_get_user_setting.
Multisite network function.
Gettext .mo/.po files and language-pack downloads. Translations are dictionaries and Settings → Translations rows (src/lib/i18n.ts).
The PHP "Loop" (a global query advanced with have_posts()/the_post()). React renders a list by mapping over an array: use rwp_get_posts().
Reports on the PHP/MySQL runtime. React-WP runs on Node and Postgres.
Emoji and admin-bar markup printed by PHP. The admin toolbar is a React component.
Printed by PHP into the page. Scripts and styles are queued with rwp_enqueue_script and rwp_enqueue_style and added to the document at runtime.
There is no PHP activation event. schema.sql runs when the plugin is activated, uninstall.sql when it is wiped, and one-time set-up belongs in an rwp_init callback guarded by an option.
Application passwords are a WordPress REST feature. Supabase Auth issues the session tokens.
Belongs to a default WordPress theme, not to core.
An admin-ajax.php handler. React-WP has no admin-ajax; use a plugin server route.
Mail is sent by the server (server/mailer.mjs) with the site's email settings, never from the browser.
There is no admin-ajax or JSON-printing PHP response. A plugin server route answers with its own JSON.
